## Seat review — ⭐ **ACCEPT**, and it falsified one of my acceptance criteria correctly.

`domain:ui` PM seat, `session_01UzHd6hDYatoDn17BuwKxnZ`. Reviewed at source on the branch, ⛔ not on the report. Merge-base `567f370` via `git merge-base`.

## ⛔ My acceptance criterion was wrong

I wrote: *"a node with no `type` attribute is byte-identical to today (regression guard)."* ⛔ **False, and unavoidably so.** Reversing the spread moves `type` from the **first** key to the **last**, so `JSON.stringify` of a parsed tree emits the same pairs in a different order. `provenance.test.ts` pinned that order and went red.

I asked for byte-identity from a change whose entire mechanism is reordering an object literal. The key **set**, every **value**, the children and the html-tier marker are unchanged — which is the guarantee I actually meant — but "byte-identical" was the wrong words for it, and the dev was right not to quietly satisfy them.

⭐ **And the handling is better than the criterion was.** The pin was **updated to the new order with the reason written beside it**, ⛔ not relaxed to a sorted comparison:

> *"this line is the one visible consequence of that reversal, and it is here rather than adjusted away because **an order pin that silently follows the implementation pins nothing**."*

That is the same principle as a control that must be able to fail, applied to a pin. Relaxing it to `sort()` would have made it green forever and worthless. The reordering is also called out in the changeset for consumers that diff serialised trees, which is where a downstream reader would actually meet it.

## The port, verified at source

```ts
const DISCRIMINATOR_ATTR = 'type';
if (name === DISCRIMINATOR_ATTR) { this.error('forbidden-attr', `Attribute "type" is not allowed on <${tag}> — …`) }
const node: SchemaElement = markHtmlTierNode({ ...props, type: tag });
```

| requirement | verdict |
|---|---|
| existing `forbidden-attr`, ⛔ no new code | ✅ — and the docblock explains it is **load-bearing**, not lazy: objectstack's lockstep holds the two code sets equal |
| one diagnostic naming **both** tag and attribute | ✅ objectstack's message, verbatim |
| `markHtmlTierNode` wrapper kept, spread reversed **inside** | ✅ |
| ⛔ no `specType` rescue (objectui#2880) | ✅ — and the docblock records *why*, including that it is not fixable at the warning layer because `type` is deliberately in `validate.ts`'s `BASE_PROPS` |
| step 4 (objectstack re-record) named, not done | ✅ |

⭐ **The new provenance pin is better than what I asked for.** I asked that the marking survive the reversal; it pins that at every depth **and** for the degenerate `{ ...{}, type: tag }` propless case — reasoning that the wrapper is the objectui-only edit and therefore the one place this port could silently drop the stamp. That is the right instinct about where a port breaks.

## The three-way ablation is the best evidence in this PR

| leg | result |
|---|---|
| baseline | `type=flex`, `codes=["forbidden-attr"]`, 17/17 green |
| **A — step 2 alone** (spread reversed, refusal removed) | `type=flex`, `codes=[]` — the authored value gone with **zero diagnostics**: the **silent discard** the card predicted |
| **B — step 1 alone** (refusal kept, old order) | indistinguishable through the public API — which is *why* the order fix is documented as defense in depth rather than sold as the fix |
| **C — both removed** (today's `main`) | **`type=GRID`**, `codes=[]` — the **silent overwrite**: a grid rendering where the author wrote a flex |

⇒ each step's contribution is measured separately, and leg C is the defect this card exists to close, reproduced.

## Stop conditions — both cleared, both with honest instrument handling

**Fixture sweep: CLEAN.** Exactly **one** html-tier document in the repo authors a `type` attribute, and it is a deliberate **negative control** asserting the spelling does not work. ⭐ The sweep regex is proven non-vacuous *because* it found that control. `examples/**`, `content/docs/**`, the schema catalog and the console's own html-tier authoring example are all clear.

**`check:sdui-lockstep`: GREEN both directions, measured.** ⭐ And the way it was measured matters: a bare run in the reference checkout exits **3 = PREREQUISITE NOT MET** (no `node_modules`), which is ⛔ **not a reading** — so it was run from a faithful scratch copy with a resolvable toolchain, `--self-test` exit 0 and the gate exit 0. For the half the gate structurally cannot see, objectstack's **own** `fingerprintOf` was run against this branch and against `origin/main`: grammar-region blob byte-identical before and after, diagnostic-code list identical, this PR adds **no** code.

## ⭐ Two findings worth more than the PR

**1. objectstack#17645 — the lockstep has drifted again, and it is latent.** objectui `main` carries **26** diagnostic codes to objectstack's **24** (`inert-quick-add` from objectui#8285, `member-type-mismatch` from objectui#8067), all landed **after** the 2026-09-05 record — i.e. inside the blind spot `check-sdui-lockstep`'s own header names. Green today because the gate compares objectstack against the record; it will red at the next `.objectui-sha` bump, **with or without this PR**. ⭐ Measured with objectstack's own extractor, and the control **pre-exists the change and is the same kind as the subject**: the same extractor on objectui at the **pinned** revision returns 24 and the matching file list, so it is demonstrably sensitive to exactly this drift. That is the control discipline this seat got wrong twice today, done right.

**2. A `packages/*/src` glob produced a FALSE ZERO, and it nearly changed the outcome.** Checking whether AGENTS.md's English-only rule describes the tree, the first probe reported **0** files with CJK comments; a proper walk reported **743** (60,233 characters). ⚠️ That is lane fact ㉑ — *a `git grep` pathspec glob matches the whole path, not a directory prefix* — hitting live, and the dev reports it nearly removed a verbatim ruling quote on the strength of that zero. ⭐ Reporting the near-miss rather than only the corrected number is what makes the number trustworthy.

## The open question, and my call

Keeping the verbatim Chinese ruling quote (option **A**) is right and I am accepting it. The reasoning holds: a **translated ruling can drift from what was decided**, whereas an English gloss is recoverable from the ADR — so the irreversible error is the translation, not the quote. And the rule as written has **743 counterexamples in the tree**, so it does not currently describe the repo.

⛔ **Not mine to settle beyond this PR:** AGENTS.md is a governed surface, so amending commandment #-1 to carve out verbatim ruling quotes (the dev's option C) is the maintainer's. Routing it as a **low-priority** note, ⛔ not a blocking decision — nothing here waits on it.

## Contract review

**Reviewed head:** `400737e` · **Card:** objectui#7235 (`Part of`)

### ① Derived judgments
This **NARROWS** the accepted grammar: the parser begins refusing a `type=` attribute it accepts today, on the html tier only. That is a deliberate, maintainer-ruled narrowing (2026-09-01, ADR-0080 amendment), ported from objectstack#13957 which already landed the same refusal upstream — so the two copies **converge** rather than diverge. ⛔ No new diagnostic code is minted (the existing `forbidden-attr` is reused, which is what holds the lockstep's code-set equality). ⛔ `@objectstack/spec` untouched. The node's key **set** and values are unchanged; only key **order** moves, disclosed in the changeset.

### ② Semver
Two released packages, one changeset, `check-changeset-presence` exit 0. A narrowing that rejects a spelling which today **silently renders the wrong component** — so no correct document becomes invalid. ⛔ No `major`.

**PASS.** Stripping `needs:contract-review` from both carriers — PR objectui#9125 and card objectui#7235 — citing this record and the judged head. `--pair 9125` exit **0**, both carriers agreeing, hung additively with a read-back.
